learningObjectives.text: Explain this episode: Where is Heracles’ pyre built?
Use the cited passage to explain: What does apotheosis mean in this episode?

main.author: Pseudo-Apollodorus
main.locator: Library 2.7.7, the pyre and reception among the gods; book 2 · chapter 7 · section 7, normalized characters 2438-2965
main.excerpt: he came of age, proceeded to Mount Oeta, in the Trachinian territory, and there constructed a pyre, mounted it, and gave orders to kindle it. When no one would do so, Poeas, passing by to look for his flocks, set a light to it. On him Hercules bestowed his bow. While the pyre was burning, it is said that a cloud passed under Hercules and with a peal of thunder wafted him up to heaven. Thereafter he obtained immortality, and being reconciled to Hera he married her daughter Hebe, by whom he had sons, Alexiares and Anicetus.
main.note: Verbatim local text with whitespace normalized. Lesson analysis is interpretation, not part of this quotation.

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: The poisoned garment causes Heracles unbearable suffering. He has a pyre built on Mount Oeta; the Library then tells of his ascent to heaven, reconciliation with Hera, and marriage to Hebe. Apotheosis means reception into divine life, not survival by ordinary healing.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “he came of age, proceeded to Mount Oeta, in the Trachinian territory, and there constructed a pyre, mounted it, and gave orders to kindle it. When no one would do so, Poeas, passing by to look for his flocks, set a light to it. On him Hercules bestowed his bow. While the pyre was burning, it is said that a cloud passed under Hercules and with a peal of thunder wafted him up to heaven. Thereafter he obtained immortality, and being reconciled to Hera he married her daughter Hebe, by whom he had sons, Alexiares and Anicetus.”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: Apotheosis answers a life too extreme for normal categories, but it does not erase the violence or pain that came before.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Apotheosis names a change of status into divine life, not an ordinary recovery from injury. Cite Library 2.7.7 for this ending; the Epitome’s Trojan returns are not the relevant passage.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: Ask what a source believes can repair or transform a damaged heroic life.

quiz.explanation: The Library says Heracles built the pyre on Mount Oeta in Trachis.

quiz.prompt: What does apotheosis mean in this episode?

choices.text: Heracles remains mortal but is released from Eurystheus’ service.
Heracles is received among the gods.
Heracles becomes a hero honoured only through a tomb.

quiz.explanation: Here the Library describes Heracles’ ascent, immortality, reconciliation with Hera, and marriage to Hebe.
